name: Bell Semiconductor
old_description: Bell Semiconductor is the successor in interest to the intellectual property portfolio that originated at Bell Labs following the invention of the transistor.  Semiconductor-related R&D continued as Bell Labs became part of Lucent Technologies, and then subsequently continues as a core competency of successor companies: Agere Systems, LSI, Avago and Broadcom.
about:
Bell Semiconductor, based in Chicago, Illinois, is the successor in interest to the intellectual property portfolio that originated at Bell Labs following the invention of the transistor. The company continues the semiconductor-related R&D lineage that passed through Lucent Technologies, Agere Systems, LSI, Avago, and Broadcom. Key leaders include Chad Hilyard and Sailesh Merchant, who previously held leadership roles in intellectual property businesses at Lucent, Agere Systems, and LSI.

The company manages and licenses a portfolio of semiconductor patents and intellectual property that enables continued integration of semiconductor technology. The inventions captured in this portfolio power every hi-tech market, including smartphones, PCs, tablets, wearables, and IoT devices. Its IP is used by foundries and integrated device manufacturers across the industry.

The portfolio is presently licensed, was previously licensed, or is currently being used by virtually all foundries and integrated device manufacturers in the semiconductor manufacturing industry, serving the broader hi-tech market.

The company's portfolio traces directly to Bell Labs, where the transistor was invented, giving it a foundational role in semiconductor technology evolution.
